class.name: NetwPredict
class.brief_description: The enum vocabulary of the prediction family, on a leaf nobody has to import an engine to read.
class.description: Every value a prediction setting is written with. [NetwPredictionHandle] is where a game writes and reads them, and this class exists so naming one costs nothing, because nothing here holds state and nothing here can be constructed. [codeblock] entity.prediction.archetype = NetwPredict.ARCHETYPE_SOLVER_BODY entity.prediction.recovery_policy = NetwPredict.RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER [/codeblock] The schedule, the restore and the mode an entity runs in are [NetwSimulationHandle] values. [b]What a game declares[/b] - [enum Archetype] what kind of body this is, which presets the rest - [enum RecoveryPolicy] what a recovery is allowed to do - [enum MissingInput] what the server does about an input that never came - [enum BreachResponse] what happens on a contact outside the prediction - [enum Reconcile] whether a selection is corrected together or apart [b]What the session reports back[/b] - [enum DriveKind] how the last drive chose its input - [enum ConsumeAction] what a consume pass did this frame - [enum ContactClass] what the local solve reported touching - [enum CommandOrigin] where one replayed input came from - [enum ExactVerdict] whether fingerprints have been compared yet - [enum Domain] whether a transition is judged by fingerprint or by tolerance - [enum TriggerShape] what asked for a recovery - [enum Attribution] what a divergence is blamed on - [enum Operator] what wrote the body during a recovery - [enum OperatorOutcome] what a recovery attempt achieved - [enum EpisodeState] how far a divergence episode has got

constants.constant: The unacknowledged span, in transitions, past which the prediction governor stops speculating and holds. A hard limit rather than something to tune. It is a quarter of the 256 transitions the engine records, so how far ahead an entity may run can never outrun the record a recovery would replay against. Read it beside [member NetwPredictionHandle.ack_age_ticks].
The solve reported no collider. A [enum ContactClass] is kept for reading afterwards and is never compared between peers.
The collider is the support reported by the declared ground sensor.
Static geometry other than the declared support.
A dynamic entity this peer predicts or simulates authoritatively.
A dynamic entity this peer neither predicts nor selects.
A kinematic or animated collision proxy.

This peer's own guess for an entity it does not own. A group replaying its members together replays them from these, so the origin is what says whether a replay reproduced what a player actually did or repeated a guess.
The authoring peer's own command, relayed through the server.
No drive has run yet.
A newly authored input label drove the simulation.
The previous input label drove the simulation again.
The consume cursor held past its buffer, so nothing drove the simulation this tick.
The consume cursor had no input queued at all, so nothing drove the simulation this tick.
A fresh input drove after older eligible labels were folded away.
A missing input label drove through [code]missing_policy[/code].
A command this peer predicted for an entity it does not own drove the simulation, so the owner never authored the input the transition ran.

No field that can trigger was past its own tolerance. The fingerprints can still disagree while every field sits inside its tolerance, so a recovery can be prepared with nothing having asked for one. A [enum TriggerShape] records what the triggering fields looked like when the recovery was judged. The distinction that matters is whether the recovery could write any of them. A write returning a withheld field and a writable one did repair something, while a write whose every trigger was withheld repaired nothing.
At least one field past its epsilon is one a sub-teleport restore may write.
Every field past its epsilon is one no sub-teleport restore may write.
A queued transition is available past the buffer being held, so it runs.
Transitions are queued but not yet past the buffer, so the pass waits.
Nothing is queued at all, so the pass has no command to run.
Nobody has compared fingerprints for this transition yet.
The two independently recorded fingerprints are equal.
The two independently recorded fingerprints differ.
With no input, the entity does not move.
Carry the last input forward over the gap.

No preset, so every setting keeps its own default until something declares it. An archetype is a starting point rather than a limit. Writing one applies its settings, and anything declared afterwards overrides what it applied. No archetype sets a [enum BreachResponse], because that decides whether a body stops predicting at all, and a preset choosing it would change the most visible behaviour an entity has with no game file saying so.

A body whose step is ordinary code and can be re-run inside one frame. It sets [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_TICK], [constant MISSING_INPUT_STALL] and [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_REPLAY], because a velocity that comes straight from the input catches up again on the next tick.

A body the physics engine solves, whose step cannot be re-run once per input. It sets [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_FRAME], [constant MISSING_INPUT_REPEAT_LAST], [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER] and [constant NetwSimulationHandle.RESTORE_EXTRAPOLATED], with a teleport distance sized for a body that settles through contacts.

Restore the acknowledged state and replay every unacknowledged input over it, which reaches the present through the entity's own simulation. [member NetwPredictionHandle.recovery_policy] is where an entity declares one, and it names what the entity wants rather than how the engine does it. A [RigidBody3D] or [RigidBody2D] at [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_FRAME] recovers under [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER] and warns once. The engine applies its forces only when the space steps, and nothing steps the space between replayed inputs.
Restore the acknowledged state and write the correction directly, with no replay.
Do not predict at all. Simulate only where the input is already authoritative, and draw what arrives everywhere else.
Report the divergence and write nothing. An entity under this policy can hold an episode open for as long as it keeps diverging, and it can never oscillate between corrections, because it makes none.

Pick from the body. A [RigidBody3D] or [RigidBody2D] recovers under [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER] and any other body under [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_REPLAY]. This is the default, and [method NetwPredictionHandle.resolved_recovery_policy] returns the pick.
Correct each predicted entity on its own.

Restore and replay this entity together with the entities its [member NetwEntity.simulation] selects. The engine admits the group when the selection commits, where every member's schedule is known. An authoritative row a member receives here is where a replay starts from rather than somewhere to jump to. The group replays from one floor, so a member that snapped to wherever its own extrapolated row landed would enter that replay from a state no other member's history knows about. The unextrapolated payload is the basis, and the pass re-runs the transitions the extrapolation was standing in for.

Keep predicting and let an ordinary recovery absorb whatever divergence follows. Touching the unmoving world is never a breach, because every peer solves against the same world. A breach is contact with a moving body this peer does not simulate, whose drawn pose is a stand-in the solve cannot reproduce.
Follow authority immediately while commands continue to flow.
The episode is still taking in comparisons and the results of recovery attempts.
A verified agreement run retired the episode.
Bounded recovery evidence was exhausted.
No later comparison has judged the write yet.
A later comparison strictly reduced or closed the aligned error.
The verification window held or grew the aligned error.
The write introduced a realized boundary absent on authority.

Every field that asked for this recovery was one the recovery was declared never to write, so the error it holds belongs to the declaration rather than to the operator. It is recorded beside [constant OPERATOR_OUTCOME_FAILED_TO_CONTRACT] rather than as a kind of it, because the two look identical from outside and mean opposite things. One is an operator that tried and did not shrink the error, and the other is an operator that was forbidden to touch it. Spending an episode's evidence on the second turns a gap in the declaration into a breach, and a breach into a demotion, which leaves the game worse off than declaring nothing at all.

The evidence needed to blame a boundary was absent. Every other [enum Attribution] names the first thing the two runs disagreed about, and [signal NetwPredictionHandle.divergence_detected] carries it.
The peers entered the transition with different declared state.
Authority ran input the owner did not author.
The transition ran against unequal world facts.
The execution topology or body mode differed.
The declared state agreed but the optional raw execution bits differed.
Equal inputs produced a different contact.
Everything observed going in agreed and the produced state still differed.
Nothing wrote the body since the preceding transition. An [enum Operator] is what an episode records for each recovery attempt.
A projected authoritative state was restored.
An exact authoritative state was restored.
A teleport restored every declared field.
The body was moved to where it should be now, across a path [member NetwPredictionHandle.transport_corridor] cleared.
The body was seeded from authority after a fallback.
The first comparison after a reseed aligned the acknowledgement.
A witnessed breach stopped prediction while input keeps flowing.
A divergence in velocity alone was left to fade with no write.
A joint pass restored the whole group to its shared starting transition.
Everything the transition read is declared equal on both peers, so its fingerprints must match exactly.
Something the transition read is declared unequal or unknown, so it is compared by tolerance.
